body.statement:
Suppose \(s=1\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and use the notation in the
definition of \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}\).  Write
\(\Delta_H^D(t)=E_P[\widehat\Delta_{j,H}^D(t)]\), which is independent
of \(j\), and define
\[
 \mathcal E_1=\left\{
 \max_{t\in\mathcal G_H}
 \left|\widehat\Delta_{1,H}^{D}(t)-\Delta_H^D(t)\right|
 \le\frac{\kappa_n}{16}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
 P(\mathcal E_1^c)
 \le2N_H\exp\{-2^{-11}mH\kappa_n^2\},
 \qquad N_H\le1+32/H,
\]
every retained \(H\)-neighborhood is contained in
\([c_P-2H,c_P+2H]\) on \(\mathcal E_1\), and, for every
\(u\ge16/n\),
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_1\bigr)
 \le9\exp\{-2^{-16}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Put \(f(x)=E_P[D\mid X=x]\).  By
\(\textnormal{ass:observable-holder-extensions}\) at \(s=1\), the two
one-sided extensions are \(M\)-Lipschitz.  Let
\(a=f(c_P-)\), \(d=f(c_P+)-f(c_P-)=d_P\), and define
\[
 e(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 f(x)-a,&x<c_P,\\
 f(x)-a-d,&x\ge c_P.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two pieces vanish at \(c_P\).  Hence each is \(M\)-Lipschitz on
its side, and, if \(x<c_P<y\),
\(|e(y)-e(x)|\le M(y-c_P)+M(c_P-x)=M(y-x)\).  Thus \(e\) is globally
\(M\)-Lipschitz and
\[
 f(x)=a+d\mathbf 1\{x\ge c_P\}+e(x).
 \tag{1}
\]
Uniformity of \(X\), from
\(\textnormal{ass:uniform-running-variable}\), and the moment
\(\int_0^1K_0=1\) give
\[
 \Delta_H^D(t)
 =d\left(1-\frac{|t-c_P|}{H}\right)_++Q_e(t),
 \qquad
 Q_e(t)=\frac1H\int_0^H\{e(t+x)-e(t-x)\}\,dx.
 \tag{2}
\]
The Lipschitz property yields
\[
 |Q_e(t)|\le MH,
 \qquad
 |Q_e(t)-Q_e(q)|\le2M|t-q|.
 \tag{3}
\]
There is a point \(q\in\mathcal G_H\) with
\(|q-c_P|\le H/64\), including at the trimmed endpoints.  Since
\(d\ge\kappa_n\) by
\(\textnormal{ass:local-compliance-strength}\) and
\(MH=\kappa_n/2^{12}\), (2)--(3) imply
\[
 \Delta_H^D(q)
 \ge\frac{63}{64}\kappa_n-\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{|t-c_P|\ge H}|\Delta_H^D(t)|
 \le\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}}.
 \tag{4}
\]

For fixed \(t\), one summand in
\(\widehat\Delta_{1,H}^D(t)\) has absolute value at most \(H^{-1}\)
and second moment at most \(2H^{-1}\).  Its centered version is bounded
by \(2H^{-1}\).  The elementary Bernstein calculation
\[
 P\{|m^{-1}\textstyle\sum_{i\in F_1}(W_i-EW_i)|>x\}
 \le2\exp\left\{-\frac{mx^2}{4/H+4x/(3H)}\right\}
 \tag{5}
\]
follows from independence in \(\textnormal{ass:iid-sampling}\) and
\(e^z\le1+z+z^2/[2(1-|z|/3)]\) for \(|z|<3\).  At
\(x=\kappa_n/16\le1\), (5) is at most
\(2\exp\{-2^{-11}mH\kappa_n^2\}\).  The union bound over
\(N_H\) grid points proves the first display of the lemma.  On
\(\mathcal E_1\), (4) and two deviations of size
\(\kappa_n/16\) show that no point at distance at least \(H\) can be
within \(\kappa_n/8\) of the empirical maximum.  Thus every retained
center is within \(H\) of \(c_P\), proving the asserted containment of
their \(H\)-neighborhoods.

It remains to control the local maximizer.  From (2)--(3), for
\(|t-c_P|\le H\),
\[
 \Delta_H^D(c_P)-\Delta_H^D(t)
 \ge\left(\frac{\kappa_n}{H}-2M\right)|t-c_P|
 \ge\frac{\kappa_n}{2H}|t-c_P|,
 \tag{6}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(H=\kappa_n/(2^{12}M)\).  For
\(H\le|t-c_P|\le2H\), the same equations give a loss at least
\(\kappa_n/2\).  Let \(c_n\) be a point of
\(\mathcal G_n(\mathcal A_H)\) within \(1/n\) of \(c_P\).  The
Lipschitz constant of the right side of (2) is at most
\(2\kappa_n/H+2M\), so, whenever \(u\ge16/n\), the grid error is
absorbed by one quarter of the lower bound in (6).

For completeness, the maximal calculation needed here is obtained
directly from (5), without a union bound over the \(1/n\) mesh.  For
\(t>c_n\), the difference between the two kernel weights is supported
on the three moving boundary strips at \(c_n-H,c_n,c_n+H\); the middle
strip has coefficient two and the other two have coefficient one.
Up to distance \(r\), its squared weight therefore integrates to at
most \(6r/H^2\), and its absolute weight is at most \(2/H\).  Reveal
the observations in each strip in increasing \(X\)-order.  Applying
the exponential bound used in (5) at the first crossing of the line
\(\kappa_n r/(8H)\) gives, on the dyadic block
\(2^ju\le r<2^{j+1}u\),
\[
 P\left\{
 \sup_{2^ju\le t-c_n<2^{j+1}u}
 \bigl[(\overline\Delta_H^D-E\overline\Delta_H^D)(t)
 -(\overline\Delta_H^D-E\overline\Delta_H^D)(c_n)\bigr]
 \ge\frac{\kappa_n2^ju}{8H}
 \right\}
 \le2e^{-2^{-13}m\kappa_n^2 2^ju}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the product conditional moment-generating function before the
first crossing is bounded by
\(\exp\{12m\lambda^2(2^{j+1}u)/H^2\}\); choosing
\(\lambda=\kappa_nH/2^7\), and using \(\kappa_n\le1/8\), gives (7).
The same argument in decreasing \(X\)-order handles \(t<c_n\).
Summing the two geometric series in \(j\), and using (6) outside the
first block, gives
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_1\bigr)
 \le9e^{-2^{-16}m\kappa_n^2u}.
\]
For \(u>2H\) the event on the left is empty by the containment already
proved.  This establishes the claimed bound for every \(u\ge16/n\).
